## 보관 원문

> # Strategic selection of a pre-reduction reactor for HPSR
>
> Adami, Hoffelner, Zarl, and Schenk published this open-access review in
> Processes on 2025-02-05 (DOI 10.3390/pr13020420).
>
> The HPSR reactor is described as a gas-tight direct-current electric-arc
> furnace at slight overpressure. The molten bath is the anode and a hollow
> graphite electrode is the cathode; ore fines and plasma gases are charged
> through the cathode. Argon stabilizes the plasma.
>
> The existing demonstration plant is described as having 200 kg ore capacity
> per trial and TRL 5. SuSteel follow-up aims to transform batch operation into
> continuous operation at 200 kg ore per hour. These are the authors' stage
> assessment and target, not independently certified current performance.
>
> Hot off-gas contains unreacted hydrogen and sensible heat. The proposed
> scaled process therefore uses HPSR off-gas for ore preheating and
> pre-reduction to improve hydrogen and thermal utilization and reduce plasma
> reactor residence time, refractory wear, and electrode consumption. The
> authors compare fluidized-bed, cyclone-cascade, and rotary-kiln options and
> propose a cyclone cascade of at least three stages.
>
> The scenario assumes about 25 vol.% argon for arc stabilization and an
> approximate thermodynamic maximum HPSR hydrogen utilization of 40 vol.% for
> liquid wustite-to-iron reduction. The paper notes that argon heating adds
> energy demand, graphite-cathode wear can introduce CO and CO2, and too little
> hydrogen in continuous operation would accumulate iron oxide in the reactor.
